disease_label_per_paper: Sjogren's syndrome with distal renal tubular acidosis presenting as hypokalaemic paralysis
presentation_summary: 23-year-old woman presented with generalized weakness, paresis and fatigue for 4 days, with polyuria, nocturia, dysuria, nausea, vomiting and fever.
Review of systems revealed dry eyes, dry mouth, thirst, itching and dental hygiene problems; exam showed xerosis of eyes and mouth, dental caries and positive Schirmer test.
Labs showed potassium 2 mEq/L, bicarbonate 14.1 mEq/L, pH 7.34, urine pH 6.5 with positive urine anion gap, anti-SSA 191.7 RU/mL, anti-SSB >200 RU/mL and positive ANA.

observations.source_text_value: chief complaints of generalised weakness, paresis and fatigue since 4 days
dryness of eyes; xerosis of eyes noted
dryness of mouth; xerosis of mouth noted
problems with dental hygiene; dental caries were noted
Schirmer test showed positive results (<10 mm of wetting in 5 min)
urinalysis showed urine pH of 6.5 with positive urine anion gap during metabolic acidosis

confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The test report was strongly suggestive of Sjogren's syndrome.
